- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% if price has recently dipped.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); add 1–3% buffer to forecast for 7–14 days post-spike.  
- If 3–5 consecutive days of low sentiment (≤0.2) follow a price drop, model often fails to recover; forecast should be slightly above recent low for next 7 days.  
- Model shows persistent lag in price recovery after mean reversion; if history shows 3+ consecutive days of price below 50% of 30-day moving average, forecast should be 1–2% above that level for next 5 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3+), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
